Q1: The paper's own measure works on Qwen where sampled naming does not. In every block the concept's log-probability at the report position rises above what random directions reach, at 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L24–38/default), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L24–38/‘word’), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 7/9 for the full vector (L32–38/default), 9/9 doses for the pure J-lens vector and 8/9 for the full vector (L32–38/‘word’). Proposal A1: make R1′ (with R1) the primary report measure and keep sampled naming as a secondary column.
Q2: No. The ‘word’ prefill does not remove Qwen's default answer: “apple” stays the top next word in the clean run and under weak injections, and sampled naming stays far below the 0.25 bar (best 0.15, pure J-lens vector, L24–38/‘word’). Qwen appears to have a canned answer for “the thought is about”. Proposal A2: keep the protocol's default prefill (the paper's), and treat naming as secondary.
Q3: The rule keeps band L32–38. The wide band L24–38 gives a much larger report effect for the full vector (3.80 vs 1.45 nats at its best dose, default prefill), but it also disturbs the neutral prompt more (KL 0.96 vs 0.28), and the pre-registered rule required a larger effect without a larger KL. This is a real trade-off: L24–38 buys a bigger report signal at the price of broader disruption. Proposal A3: L32–38 as registered; you may prefer L24–38 for signal, and the pilot gives you both.
Q4: Yes. With the grid extended down to 1/256, every block has a dose range where the non-J part leaves the report untouched: onset s* = 1/64 (L24–38/default), 1/128 (L24–38/‘word’), 1/64 (L32–38/default), 1/128 (L32–38/‘word’). The reader doses by the rule would be 1/256, 1/64, 1/16 for L32–38/default. Proposal A4: the 9-point grid for every model-side measure. Those reader doses would give all-zero reads (Q5), so A5 moves the text readers to 1/64, 1/4 and 1.
Q6: Yes, unlike the 2-concept smoke: in all four blocks the design's clamp removes more of the non-J part's report effect than the random clamp does (L24–38/default +0.81 nats [0.39, 1.26], 9 concepts; L24–38/‘word’ +0.83 nats [0.34, 1.32], 9 concepts; L32–38/default +0.62 nats [0.26, 1.03], 9 concepts; L32–38/‘word’ +0.63 nats [0.29, 0.97], 9 concepts). Caveat: this clamp runs to L62, where a concept's J direction approaches its output direction, so part of the effect may be the clamp blocking the answer itself. Step 7b's band-limited re-entry clamp (Q10) tests that.
Q7: Few splits leak. With the rule fixed beforehand, band L32–38 has no leaky concepts and band L24–38 has earth, soap. Proposal A10: exclude these from every non-J contrast in the full run (earth is a dev concept; soap is a test concept and would be excluded before any test outcome exists).
Q8: The baseline matters somewhat: the median cosine between the two concept-vector versions is 0.851 (lowest 0.43), below the 0.9 line. Leave-one-out stays primary and the 194-word version becomes a mandatory sensitivity check (A12).
M1_preview: Preview only (dev concepts, no test): at matched norm the J part beats the non-J part at low and middle doses (up to +0.55 nats at L32–38/default) and loses at high doses (down to −0.50). The two reach similar peaks; the J part gets there at a lower dose.
Q5: Both text readers name the planted concept when they are handed the written cell, and neither sees it at the report position at their usual layers (L40–44). On direct reads at s = 1 (band L32–38) the NLA names the full vector in 78% of samples and the non-J part in 60%; the Oracle names the non-J part in up to 90%. At the report position the highest naming rate for any planted condition, reader, dose and band is 8%. The reader-free probe agrees (it never classifies the report position as the concept at L42), so this is the concept not having arrived there, not the readers missing it. As posed, P11a and P11b compare the readers with the model at a position the content does not reach by the readers' layers. Step 8 (Q12, Q13) checks later layers.
P17_preview: Preview of P17 (dev only, not a test): on direct reads the Oracle names the non-J part at least as often as the NLA (s = 1: Oracle up to 90%, NLA 60%; s = 1/4: Oracle up to 15%, NLA 0%). That runs against the A.9.2-based expectation that the Oracle sees content outside J-space less. At s = 1/4 both readers name the J part far more often than the non-J part (Oracle up to 53% vs 15%), the same dose pattern as the model's report.
budget: The fast float32-residual regime matches the exact SEC replay on 100% of 270 cells (median log-prob difference 0.030 nats), so the full run can use it throughout (A13).
Q10: The clamp's specificity lives at the output end. Run all the way to L62, the re-entry clamp removes much more of the non-J part's report effect than its random null (L32–38: +0.87 nats [0.41, 1.39]; L24–38: +1.19 nats [0.58, 1.83]). Stopped at L44 it removes nothing beyond its null (L32–38: −0.03 nats [−0.11, 0.07]; L24–38: −0.31 nats [−0.56, −0.03], the random clamp even removing slightly more). The concept's J direction turns into its output direction with depth (median cosine 0.38 at L40, 0.47 at L44, 0.77 at L52, 0.92 at L62), so a clamp reaching the late layers blocks the answer itself. By the pre-registered reading: no evidence on these dev concepts that the non-J part's effect on the report is mediated by re-entry into the concept's J coordinates within the workspace layers. A clamp that reaches the late layers could produce the paper's result (the non-J effect falling to about zero) without any workspace re-entry, so a full-range clamp alone cannot separate the two. Proposal A8: if M2 stays, run it as a band-limited re-entry clamp with its null, and report the full-range version only next to the cosine curve. Step 10 (Q14) then located where along the depth the clamp starts to act.
Q11: No, in either band. At every dose where the non-J part moves the model's report, the concept's median J-lens rank at the report position stays in the hundreds to thousands at every layer up to L62; the full vector and the J part behave the same, and so do the logit lens and the R-lens. Planting shifts the report distribution toward the concept without the concept ever becoming a top candidate at the report position, consistent with the readers (Q5) and the absolute probe criterion.
rlens: The R-lens and J-lens agree closely on these reads (Spearman 0.82, top-10 agreement 98%), so for planted concepts the two Jacobian lenses are interchangeable as token readers; adding R-lens to the full run costs little and answers the consistency question directly (A14).
Q12: Read with care. By the pre-registered rule (probe response above the strongest of five random directions), every condition “arrives” at the report position by L32–34 at every dose, even 1/256, so all three registered predictions technically came true. That rule is degenerate: the forward pass is deterministic and nearly linear at these doses, so the comparison with random directions is scale-free and fires at any dose. By the absolute criterion (the probe classifies the read as the concept), the concept never reaches the report position at any layer L32–62, for any condition, dose or band (highest rate anywhere 10%). Together with Q5 and Q11: planting nudges the model's report distribution without producing a concept state at the report position that a linear probe or a lens can read (the Oracle at late layers is the one partial exception, see Q13). P11a/P11b at the report position therefore compare the readers with the model where neither can find the concept; the amendment must re-pose P11 (proposal: compare reader sensitivity with model sensitivity on matched measures at the written cell, and drop the report-position version).
short_html:
The short version

  • Qwen reports planted concepts only by the paper's own metric. Asked “the thought is about "…"”, Qwen almost never says the planted concept: it has a canned answer (“apple”), and neither prefill removes it. But the concept's log-probability at that position rises reliably above what random directions do (Q1 yes, 4/4 blocks). The report gate as written failed; the amendment makes log-prob the report measure.
  • That metric is specific to the planted concept. The rise is not just the canned answer being displaced. At s = 1/4 the planted concept's own rise is the largest of the 10 dev concepts for 80% (L32–38) and 90% (L24–38) of concepts, against 10% by chance, and random directions stay at chance (step 10). Other words also rise, by up to about half a nat, so a specificity margin is worth reporting next to R1′.
  • No clear J-space privilege for report on these dev concepts. At equal size the J part beats the non-J part at low and middle doses, the order reverses at high doses, and the two reach similar peaks. This is a preview on 10 dev concepts, not the test (M1 runs on the 45 test concepts); the pattern holds under all five alternative J-space constructions tried (step 9).
  • The privilege clamp acts only after the readers' layers. Clamping the concept's J coordinates removes much of the non-J part's report effect, beyond a random-token clamp, when it runs to L62. It removes nothing when it stops at L44, under every J-space construction tried (step 9). Step 10 shows the specific part building up over L48–56 (reliably from L50 with band L32–38 and from L52 with L24–38) as the concept's J direction turns into its output direction. So the non-J effect reaches the answer through the concept's J coordinates only late, where those coordinates are close to the output direction itself. Up to L46 there is no sign of it.
  • The readers see the planted concept mainly when handed the written cell. On direct reads at the top dose the best reader names the full vector in 93% of samples and the non-J part in 90%. At the report position, at the readers' usual layers (L40–44), no text reader exceeds 8%; no lens puts the concept in its top 10 at any layer up to L62, and the probe never classifies it as present. Only the Oracle at its late layers (L52–60), and only with the wide band, names it there for a few concepts (up to 28% on average; the non-J part only for earth, skin, of which earth has a leaky split). The model's report shifts, but a readable concept state rarely forms where the answer is produced.
  • The readers are less sensitive than the model, not more. The model's report responds from s = 1/128 or 1/64; the first dose at which any reader names any planted condition in more than 10% of direct reads is s = 1/4. This compares a fine measure (the model's log-prob) with a coarse one (whether a reader names the concept), so it holds for these measures only; a reader-side likelihood could be more sensitive. On these concepts the NLA does not see what the model cannot use, and the Oracle reads the non-J part at least as well as the NLA (against the P17 premise).
  • A methods trap, caught. Comparing a probe with random directions at the same dose is meaningless in a deterministic forward: it ‘detects’ any planted direction at any dose. The absolute criterion is used instead (amendment A9).
  • The machinery is sound. Every write exact (ρ within 1 ± 3e-07), runs bit-identical on repeat, the fast regime matches the exact one on 100% of 270 cells, the C1–C3 checks and errata are in, and the amendment's budget for the full run is about 1.5–3 GPU hours (measured throughput, A16).

What you decide

  • The report measure (A1): log-prob at the open quote, with the paper's rank, instead of sampled naming. Step 10 found it specific to the planted concept.
  • Band (A3): L32–38 as registered, or the stronger but more disruptive L24–38. Step 10 leans weakly toward L32–38.
  • P11 (A6): drop the report-position version (nothing arrives there) for a reader-vs-model sensitivity comparison.
  • The clamp (A8): by the registered step-10 rule, the re-entry clamp runs to L50 rather than L44, with its null. I would also run the whole end-layer curve (a few GPU minutes).
  • The go for the amended full run on the 45 test concepts (about 1.5–3 GPU hours).

Everything here is development data on 10 dev concepts. None of it is a test of the pre-registered predictions; those need the amended full run.
power: Planning numbers from the 10 dev concepts. For the J-vs-non-J report contrast at s = 1/4 the predicted 95% CI half-width with 45 test concepts is ±0.24 nats at band L32–38 and ±0.69 at L24–38 (concepts vary much more in the wide band, another point for L32–38). For reader naming the spread between concepts dominates: the NLA's naming of the non-J part at s = 1 gives ±0.139 with 4 samples and ±0.137 with 8, so doubling the samples buys almost nothing; more concepts is what helps (as your review argued).
Q13: Yes by the registered rule, with two strong qualifications. First, it happens only with the wide band: at band L32–38 the Oracle at L48–60 names nothing at the report position (highest rate 0%). With band L24–38 at s = 1/4 it names the full vector at L52–60 in up to 28% of samples on average (random directions 0%). Second, the hits come from a few concepts: the full vector for earth, frame, gel, skin, storm; the non-J part only for earth, skin, and earth has a leaky split at this band (its non-J part still carries its own J-lens direction). Excluding leaky concepts as the registered rule does for non-J contrasts, the non-J part reaches the report position only for skin. So a strong enough planted concept can reach the report position in a form the Oracle reads at its late layers, but only for some concepts and only with the wider band; the NLA, fixed at L42, cannot test this.
step9: Both headline findings survive every alternative construction: F1 holds in 5 of 5 and F2 in 5 of 5 (k = 10, k = 25, LS refit, raw-W_U atoms, 194-word baseline). The J part leads at middle doses and trails at high doses in every variant; the non-J part's peak is the higher one in 5 of 5. The re-entry clamp to L62 beats its null in every variant and the clamp stopped at L44 never does. On the dev concepts these are not artifacts of how J-space was built; whether they hold on the test concepts is the amended full run's job.
Q14: By the registered rule the clamp first becomes specific at L50 with band L32–38 and at L52 with L24–38. It does not switch on at one layer. With band L32–38 the extra reduction grows steadily: −0.03 nats at L44, +0.10 [−0.01, 0.24] at L48 and +0.25 [0.08, 0.44] at L50, then a plateau from L56 (+0.86; +0.87 at L62). The growth runs in step with the concept's J atom turning toward its output direction (median cosine 0.47 at L44, 0.67 at L50, 0.85 at L56). Unclamped, the non-J part raises the concept's log-prob by 1.71 nats at these concepts' best doses. The concept clamp to L50 removes 23% of that and its random null 8%; run to L62 they remove 64% and 13%. With the wide band, the concept clamp stopped at L44 slightly raises the effect (3.68 vs 3.45 nats unclamped). That is why the band-limited clamp came out below its null in step 7b. One possible reading is that the blocks there push against the concept along its J coordinates. My reading: the non-J part's effect on the report is routed through the concept's J coordinates mainly over L48–56. That is after the band and the readers' layers (L40–44), and while those coordinates are turning into the output direction. Under the registered mapping for band L32–38, M2 runs the re-entry clamp to L50 instead of L44 (A8). The boundary is soft: at L48 the interval only just includes zero, and at L50 the atom is already two-thirds aligned with the output direction. So this is not a clean window separate from the output direction, and the whole end-layer curve is more informative than any single end layer. For the 45 test concepts it costs about 6–7 GPU minutes per band.
Q15: Yes. The log-prob rise singles out the planted concept. It is not just every word gaining as Qwen's canned answer is displaced. Clean, the open quote predicts “apple” with probability 41%, then “cat” and “banana”. For the full concept vector at s = 1/4, the planted concept's own rise is the largest of the 10 dev concepts for 80% of concepts with band L32–38 and 90% with L24–38 (chance 10%). It beats the median rise of the other 87 words by +1.42 nats [0.74, 2.16] and +3.28 nats [2.61, 3.90]. Random directions stay at chance at every dose (identification at most 14%). Every injected condition meets the rule in both bands (it needs 3 doses). The pure J-lens atom meets it at 5/9 and 7/9 doses, the full vector at 7/9 and 6/9, the J part at 5/9 and 7/9, and the non-J part at 4/9 and 3/9. Other words do rise too: for the full vector their median rise reaches 0.56 nats at the higher doses, and random directions lift them as well. So a raw ΔR1′ carries a generic part of up to about half a nat. By the registered mapping A1 stands: R1′ is the primary report measure. My suggestion, not part of the rule, is to report SM next to R1′; it removes the generic part at no cost (A18). A3: by the registered rule the wider band is not at least as specific as L32–38. At s = 1/16 it identifies 50% of concepts against 70%, though its margin is larger (0.71 vs 0.41 nats); at s = 1/4 it is ahead on both. The failing comparison rests on 2 concepts at one dose. That is weak evidence for L32–38, in the same direction as the pilot's band rule (Q3).
